From: Katie Summers <katie.summers@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-30T08:15:00-04:00
Subject: Request: Detailed performance questionnaire for RFP - Acme Financial

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our RFP process we need a completed performance questionnaire describing Redwood's latency and throughput characteristics under the following test scenarios: single-request p99 at 128/512/1024 tokens, batch throughput vs batch size (1,4,8,16), sustained QPS at 95th percentile for 15-minute windows, and cold vs warm-start behavior for KV-cached chat workloads. Please include test methodology, hardware used (GPU type, memory), quantization settings, and whether numbers are from hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.

Attached is our perf questionnaire (Acme_RFP_Perf_Qs.pdf). Can you return responses and any supporting benchmark artifacts (scripts, CSVs, methodology) by EOD Nov 3? We may ask Redwood to run a side-by-side harness with our internal tests later in the process.

Also include SLA-impacting details (tail latency under load, best-effort vs guaranteed throughput) and any recommendations for Dedicated pool sizing for a baseline load of 2000 concurrent conversational users (avg 300 tokens/user/session).

Appreciate it — Katie
Procurement, Acme Financial

Marissa / team — draft responses attached (Redwood_perf_report_v1.xlsx) and a short methodology summary below. I focused on the gen-family open LLM variants we usually reference in RFPs (quantized 4-bit where noted). Quick clarifying question for Acme: do they expect numbers from Hosted (our multi-tenant), Redwood Dedicated (dedicated GPUs), or their Private (VPC) deployment? Side-by-side runs may change throughput by ~10-20% depending on network and tenant isolation.

High-level methodology (summary):
- Hardware: A100 80GB (Dedicated runs); NVIDIA H100 80GB for short warm-up comparisons; Hosted numbers are sample aggregates across multi-tenant pools (mixed G4/H100 in us-west-2).
- Sequence lengths: tests at fixed seq lengths 128 / 512 / 1024 tokens; payload measured per request including extra metadata tokens.
- Batching: batch sizes 1/4/8/16 using our continuous batching harness with warm-up period of 5 minutes, then 15-minute steady-state window for throughput/95th/99th percentiles.
- KV-cache behavior: measured cold (empty KV) vs warm (after 50 requests) for conversational session re-use, p99 measured across sessions.
- Quantization: int4 (LLM.int4), int8 where noted — we include model artifact tags.

Preliminary numbers (percentiles in ms, throughput in tokens/sec):
- p99 @128 tokens: Hosted 110ms, Dedicated 70ms (A100), Private_est 75-90ms;
- p99 @512 tokens: Hosted 320ms, Dedicated 210ms;
- p99 @1024 tokens: Hosted 610ms, Dedicated 420ms;
- Throughput (tokens/sec) batch size 1/4/8/16 (Dedicated): 6200 / 9200 / 11800 / 14500;
- Sustained 95th QPS (15m window) (Dedicated): 1400 requests/sec for 128-token avg payload at 8k tokens/sec aggregate;
- Cold vs Warm KV: cold p99 ~2.1x warm p99; warm-state caching reduces per-request latency by ~45% depending on seq length.

Attachments include raw CSVs for the runs and the XLS with per-run detail. Connor — can you add Dedicated pool sizing notes (GPU counts and recommended buffer for 2000 concurrent conversational users)?

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Katie Summers <katie.summers@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-03T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed performance questionnaire for RFP - Acme Financial

Hi Katie — please find our completed questionnaire and supporting artifacts attached (Redwood_perf_report_v1.xlsx, perf_methodology_2025.pdf). Below is a short executive summary pulled from the attachment:

Executive summary:
- Provided environments: Hosted (multi-tenant aggregates), Redwood Dedicated (A100/H100 pools), and Private (VPC) estimated ranges. All figures include model and quantization tags.
- Tail latency (p99) examples: 70ms (A100, 128 tokens) to 420ms (A100, 1024 tokens). Hosted aggregates are higher due to mixed hardware.
- Throughput scaling: our continuous batching harness shows near-linear token/sec improvement up to batch size 16 for gen-family models; see sheet “batching_vs_size”.
- KV-cache effects: warm KV reduces p99 by ~40–50% in conversational workloads; cold starts can double tail latency in worst-case patterns.
- Recommended Dedicated sizing for baseline (2000 concurrent conversational users, avg 300 tokens/session): 8 x A100 80GB with autoscale buffer (50%) to cover traffic spikes; expected sustained throughput ~65k tokens/sec across pool with 95th QPS headroom.

We flagged any numbers derived from short H100 runs as such and included raw CSVs for independent review. If you'd like, Redwood can run a hosted vs dedicated side-by-side harness with Acme's test inputs; we'd need a 2–3 day window and access to representative prompt sets.

Next steps: please confirm whether you prefer (1) a self-run side-by-side kit we provide, (2) Redwood-conducted run in our Dedicated environment, or (3) VPC-private test support. Once you confirm, we can schedule a remote demo of the harness and set dates for the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Katie Summers <katie.summers@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-03T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed performance questionnaire for RFP - Acme Financial

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed attachments; I reviewed the XLS summary. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) Can Redwood run the side-by-side harness in Dedicated (option 2) and share the full CSVs and our exact prompt set? We want to include the results in our security/compliance packet.
2) For the Dedicated sizing recommendation (8 x A100 + 50% buffer), can you provide a short TCO note comparing that to a smaller H100 pool (e.g., 6 x H100) so we can present alternatives to infrastructure?
3) Do you have an internal runbook or audit log snippet showing how you capture per-token latency and p99 windows (we need this for the RFP evidence)?

On the side-by-side: please propose available windows next week (Nov 10–14). If feasible we will request Redwood to perform the runs and include the CSVs in our supplier evidence.

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.
